message.content:
Second independent check. Is this M12 code-review finding a REAL, actionable bug/issue that should be fixed before merge? Read the code yourself. Be skeptical — confirm only if you can point to the concrete problem in the diff.

Lens: correctness
File: components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx (cancel(id) onClick of the Cancel button)
Title: Cancel button cancels irreversibly on a single click with no confirmation
Detail: Clicking "Cancel" calls cancelBooking immediately. The action can charge the full block per the cancellation policy (cancellationOutcome → capture) when a scheduled session is within 1h of start, so an accidental single click can both cancel the booking and charge the customer. A confirmation string `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") was added to messages/en.json for exactly this but is never used.

content.text:
Confirmed on all points. The grep for `cancelConfirm` in code (`.ts`/`.tsx`) returns exit 1 with no matches, so the string exists only in `messages/en.json` and is never referenced. And `cancellationOutcome` returns `action: "charge"` (capturing the full `priceBlockCents`) whenever a scheduled session's start is within 1 hour, which `cancelBooking` turns into `payments.capture(...)`.

The behavior chain is verified:
- `UpcomingBookings.tsx:96` — `onClick={() => cancel(item.id)}` fires `cancelBooking` immediately with no intervening confirmation.
- `actions.ts:75-100` — for a `scheduled` booking inside the 1h window, `cancellationOutcome` returns `charge`, so `release` is `false`, and the code calls `payments.capture` for the full `price_block_cents`.
- `lib/pricing.ts:130-136` — confirms the within-1h capture path.
- `messages/en.json:373` — `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") exists but is referenced nowhere in code.

This is a real, actionable correctness/UX-safety issue: an irreversible, money-charging action with no confirmation step, and a confirmation string that was added for exactly this purpose but left unwired.

input.reason: Confirmed real and actionable. In components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx the Cancel button (line 96) fires `onClick={() => cancel(item.id)}`, which calls `cancelBooking(id)` immediately — there is no confirm() / Dialog / window.confirm anywhere in the component. The action is destructive AND can charge money: in app/(customer)/account/actions.ts (cancelBooking, lines 75-100), a "scheduled" booking runs cancellationOutcome(); per lib/pricing.ts (lines 130-136) when the session start is within 1h (startMs - nowMs < ONE_HOUR_MS) it returns action "charge", so `release` is false and the code calls `payments.capture({ amountCents: booking.price_block_cents })` — the full block is charged. So a single accidental click both cancels the booking and captures payment, with no undo. The fix was clearly intended: messages/en.json line 373 defines `account.cancelConfirm` = "Cancel this booking?", but a repo-wide grep over .ts/.tsx finds zero references to `cancelConfirm` (exit 1, no matches) — the confirmation string was added but never wired up. Recommended fix: gate cancel() behind a confirmation (Dialog or at minimum the existing account.cancelConfirm copy) before invoking cancelBooking, ideally surfacing that the block may be charged when within 1h. Severity is meaningful because it can move real money irreversibly on a single misclick.
